speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, can you tell me when the double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and arm weakness first started? Have these symptoms gotten worse throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, chewing, or speaking, especially later in the day? Also, have you noticed that your eyelids droop or that your facial muscles feel weak?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, chewing, or speaking, particularly later in the day? Have you also noticed that your eyelids droop or that your facial muscles feel weak?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fluctuating weakness, ptosis is a key sign to rule out, so does your vision blur when you look up, and do your eyelids droop more after prolonged use? I would also like to check your reflexes; can you describe if they feel normal, decreased, or absent? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies: Present (elevated). Vital Signs: Temperature 36.6°C (97.9°F), Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 16 breaths/min. Neurological Examination: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze; Diminished motor strength in upper extremities with normal tone; Normal reflexes; Normal sensation. Electromyography: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Chest CT: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated antibodies, ptosis that worsens with use, and decreased response on repetitive stimulation confirm your diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
